title: Integral closure commutes with finite products
statement: Let $R_i\to S_i$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings for $i=1,\dots,n$, let $R=\prod_iR_i$ and $S=\prod_iS_i$, and let $S_i'\subseteq S_i$ be the subring of elements integral over $R_i$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then the subring of $S$ consisting of elements integral over $R$ is exactly $\prod_iS_i'$. If every $R_i\to S_i$ is injective, so that $R\subseteq S$, then $R$ is integrally closed in $S$ if and only if each $R_i$ is integrally closed in $S_i$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0CY9 (lemma-finite-product-integral-closure, line 7583), using Tag 0CY8 for coordinatewise integrality

proof.text: For an integral tuple, apply IsIntegral.map_of_comp_eq to each pair of evaluation ring homomorphisms to obtain coordinatewise integrality.

Conversely choose component monic annihilating polynomials, take the finite supremum of their natural degrees, multiply each by the required power of X, and assemble the coefficients with Polynomial.piEquiv. The resulting polynomial is monic and annihilates the tuple coordinatewise; the construction also handles the empty product.

Use the coordinatewise criterion to prove the integral-closure subring equality by extensionality. Under injectivity, use isIntegrallyClosedIn_iff, single-coordinate tuples, and coordinatewise preimages to prove the equivalence of integral closedness.
